paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 11/10/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, Polymarket pays 45.25 and Kalshi 49.00. In polls with fieldwork up to 10/22, she is first in all 55 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, at 31% to 38%, and leads in the 26 runoff match-ups in which she was tested, at 52% to 70%. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation against her ineligibility is due to be ruled on by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 16.5 across 38 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days and places in the top two in 42 of the 55 lists of the last 45 days; in the 9 runoff match-ups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, at 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is at 13.50 on Polymarket and 12.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names among the top five in both markets appear in few poll lists or in none.** David Lisnard is 3rd on Polymarket, at 12.85, and at 13.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he appears in 13 of the 55 lists of the last 45 days, without placing in the top two in any of them, and averages 7.0 across 12 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days. Christine Lagarde is 5th in both markets, at 5.85 on Polymarket and 6.00 on Kalshi, and no list in the poll database tests her. She is not a declared candidate; on 10/29, the European Central Bank announced that she will leave the bank's presidency on 02/07/2027.

**Raphaël Glucksmann and Édouard Philippe tie in the poll average; in the market, they do not.** Both are at 13.9 over the last 30 days, across 36 and 27 lists, from 7 pollsters each; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe places in the top two in 10 of 39, and Glucksmann in 3 of 45. In the win contract, Philippe is at 8.50 on Polymarket and 7.20 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 2.65 and 4.00.

**In the French press on 11/10, a day after Teddy Riner announced his candidacy, six of the ten headlines collected mention him by name.** Le JDD and CNews report a poll on what the French think of his candidacy; BFMTV reports that Béatrice Bellay, a Socialist Party deputy, will give him her sponsorship signature, one of the 500 from elected officials that each candidate must gather, and covers the attacks he faces online; Ouest-France covers where he stands politically, and Le Figaro runs a column on the candidacy. In the win contract, Riner is at 2.35 on Polymarket and 1.00 on Kalshi. No voting-intention list in the structured poll database has tested him so far, and the most recent fieldwork in the database is from 10/22.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
